craft_notes: Sthāyin: turbidity-as-conceit — the rite's target named. Sanskrit-first: hi emphatic kept ('that indeed'); tadekarūpe 'pi concessive kept ('even in That'); abhimāna = conceit, not dirt (C1 crux). Rows: 9 (purity/turbidity antithesis doubled), 1 ('alien nature' closes — the other-form named last), 10 (conceit left standing, no image added). Close: 'is the conceit of admixing a form of alien nature.' Rejected: 'delusion' for conceit — killed: abhimāna is self-conceit, not moha; 'even in the One' — killed: tadekarūpe kept That-whose-form. Read aloud: WASH-ing-OFF-turb-ID-ity — THAT in-DEED is-PU-ri-ty; AND-turb-ID-i-ty, EV-en IN-That WHOSE sole-FORM is-THAT, IS the-CON-CEIT of-AD-mix-ing a-FORM of-A-li-en-NA-ture.

lines: Washing off turbidity — that indeed is purity;
and turbidity, even in That whose sole form is That,
is the conceit of admixing a form of alien nature.
l4.sanskrit_cite: kāluṣyāpagamo hi śuddhiḥ kāluṣyaṃ ca tadekarūpe 'pi atatsvabhāvarūpāntarasaṃvalanābhimānaḥ

reads_against.argmap: What counts as turbidity, and what washes it? → Impurity is not dirt but abhimāna: the conceit of a second, alien form inside the sole-formed That; its removal alone is śuddhi.
c1_essence: Purity is washing-off of turbidity; turbidity is the conceit of admixing an alien form — even in That whose sole form is That.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
